name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

areaKm2.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: Yugoslavia 255,800 km2 (mid, high). world_1960 Yugoslavia polygon = 253,152 km2 computed by the pipeline (low).

population.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: population 22,130,000 (mid). OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) Yugoslavia 1980 = 21.62M (low); COW NMC v7 tpop 1980 = 22,304k (high).

urbanization.note: World Bank WDI Database Archives, version 1991 Apr, Yugoslavia (code YUG, then the SFRY) urban share 1980 = 42.3% (mid). HYDE 3.5 via OWID (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/urbanization-last-500-years.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) present-day republics 1980: Bosnia 35.5%, Slovenia 48.0%, Croatia 50.1%, North Macedonia 53.5% (Serbia missing); range 0.36-0.46 brackets the federal value.

activePersonnel.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: total armed forces 264,000 (145,000 conscripts): army 190,000, navy 30,000 (incl. 15,000 marines), air force 44,000 (mid). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 252,500 (low; navy 17,500). High adds the 16,000 frontier guards.

trainedReserves.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 500,000 reservists (low, mid); plus 1,000,000 in the Territorial Defence Force (high). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1-3 million Territorial Defence (Partisan) and 2,000,000 Civil Defence on mobilisation, not counted.

supportPersonnel.note: Active strength outside the P roles: army 190,000 minus ~90,000 infantry = 100,000 (armour, artillery, AA, engineers, logistics); navy 30,000 minus ~8,000 marines and airborne counted as P = ~22,000 (MB 1981-82 navy 17,500); air force 44,000 (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru). 100,000 + 22,000 + 44,000 = 166,000 -> mid 160,000.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total National Defence: active 264,000 + 500,000 reserves = 764,000 (0.035 of 22.1M, low); + 1,000,000 Territorial Defence (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru) = 1.76M (0.08, mid); with the 1-3 million TDF of The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml) up to ~3.3M (0.15, high).

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Educated guess. Rifle strength of the army's 8 infantry divisions, 15-16 independent infantry brigades (incl. mechanised and 3 light) and 1 mountain brigade (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru; The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml)); army 190,000 with 130,000 conscripts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5 relative to 1980 NATO/Warsaw Pact. Evidence: domestic small arms, Sagger and Snapper ATGW, 82-105 mm RCL, SA-7 (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); few IFVs (M-980 on order).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 15-month conscription, 130,000 of 190,000 conscripts.

count.note: Educated guess. Airborne brigade and the marine brigade (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru lists 15,000 marines in the navy, The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml) 2,500 marines in one brigade of 2 regiments); mid assumes ~3,000 airborne + ~5,000 marines.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: light weapons, RCL and ATGW.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: selected volunteers and conscripts in elite brigades.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 1,500 T-34/-54/-55 and M-47 (mid) plus about 650 M-4 medium tanks (high 2,150). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1,240 T-34/-54/-55 and 60 M-47 (low 1,300), M-4 and T-34/85 in reserve storage. Some PT-76 light tanks not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: T-54/55 and many T-34 and M-47 against T-72 and M60A3 era best; domestic M-84 not yet in service.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 8 independent tank brigades of conscripts.

count.note: The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 200 BTR-50/-60/-152 (low), some M-980 MICV and some M-60 APC; The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: M-980 MICV, BTR-50/-60P/-152 and M-60 APC without counts, 700 M-980 on order. Mid and high add the uncounted M-980 and M-60.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: M-980 domestic IFV with Sagger; BTR-50/152 dated.

count.note: The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1,800 guns (M-1955 and SU-100 100 mm, 122, 130 and 152 mm) (mid); howitzers (M-48 76 mm, 105, 122, 155 mm) and 128 mm MRL listed without counts (high 2,400 allows ~600). Low 1,500 for unserviceable older pieces. 12 field artillery regiments (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Soviet 130 mm M-46 and US 155 mm alongside Second World War types; domestic 128 mm MRL.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 9 interceptor squadrons with 126 MiG-21F/PF/M (low, mid; The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml) the same); high adds the 18 MiG-21U of the conversion unit.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: MiG-21F/PF/M with AA-2 Atoll against F-15/F-16 and MiG-23 era best.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 44,000-strong air force with 7,000 conscripts (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 15 FGA squadrons with 12 Kraguj and 130 Galeb/Jastreb = 142 (low, mid); high adds the 40 Galeb/Jastreb of 3 reconnaissance squadrons. 346 combat aircraft in all.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Galeb/Jastreb light jet trainers-attack aircraft and Kraguj piston COIN; the Orao only on order (25, The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml)).

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 5 AB-205, 14 Mi-1, 18 Mi-4, 12 Mi-8, 10 Whirlwind, 20 Partizan (Gazelle) = 79 (low). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 5 AB-205, 18 Mi-4, 50 Mi-8, 5 Whirlwind, 5 Partizan, 1 A-109 = 84 (mid), plus 15 Partizan trainers (high 99).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: transport helicopters, mostly Mi-4/Mi-8; no attack helicopters (94 Partizan on order).

count.note: Educated guess. FROG-7 SSM launchers (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru lists the type without a count); one battalion assumed. Coastal Samlet batteries are counted under the navy.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: unguided FROG-7 rockets.

count.note: SAM battalions count as one battery each, AA regiments as 3-4 batteries. The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 8 SA-2 + 6 SA-3 battalions = 14 and 12 army AA artillery regiments (low 14 + 12 x 4 = 62). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 24 AA regiments under the Air Defence Force (mid 14 + 24 x 3 = 86, high 14 + 24 x 4 = 110). SA-6/-7/-9 and ZSU-23-4 with the army.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: SA-2/SA-3 static sites and SA-6/SA-9 mobile systems, many towed guns of 20-94 mm.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 1 Split-class destroyer, in reserve (low 0, mid 1). The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 1 Koni-class frigate with SA-N-4 (high 2 counts both).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: 1950s domestic destroyer; Koni a light Soviet export frigate.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 18-month naval service (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 3 corvettes, 16 FAC(M) with Styx (6 Rade Koncar, 10 Osa-I), 15 Shershen FAC(T), 19 large patrol craft and 27 minesweepers = 80 (mid); low 67 without the 13 river minesweepers. The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 3 + 16 + 15 + 20 + 30 = 84 (high). 25 coast artillery batteries with Samlet not counted.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Osa-I and Rade Koncar missile boats with Styx, effective in the Adriatic islands.

count.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 6 submarines (1 Sava, 3 Heroj, 2 Sutjeska) (low, mid); The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 7 (2 Sava) (high).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: domestic diesel-electric boats of the 1960s-70s.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: experienced Partisan-generation command and a worked-out Total National Defence doctrine combining the army with 1M+ Territorial Defence (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); never tested against a major power.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: multi-national conscript army with republic-based Territorial Defence; Tito died in May 1980 and national tensions later broke the army apart in 1991.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: defensive motivation against a Warsaw Pact invasion after Czechoslovakia 1968; conscript force.

weapons.note: Anchor: 8 (1943) toward 9 (1985). Evidence: Sagger ATGW, SA-7, 128 mm MRL and domestic small arms (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

armor.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: T-54/55 the best tank, many T-34, M-47 and M-4.

ships.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: Styx-armed Osa and Rade Koncar missile boats, Koni frigate with SA-N-4.

fortification.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: coastal artillery and Samlet batteries (25), hardened airbases and mountain shelters of Total National Defence.

logistics.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: motorised army with a domestic vehicle industry.

communications.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: radio-equipped formations of Soviet and domestic types.

isr.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: 3 reconnaissance squadrons of Galeb/Jastreb, SA-2/SA-3 radars.

air.note: Anchor: between 8 and 9. Evidence: MiG-21 interceptors and domestic Galeb/Jastreb attack jets; Orao on order.

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1990 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Global Military Spending Dataset via OWID, Yugoslavia 1980 = 3.23% (low, mid). High = The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): defence 1981 $3.47 bn / GNP 1979 $64.4 bn = 5.4%. CIA World Factbook 1990: 4.6% of national income (1989).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Industry incl. mining and construction share of output. Agriculture employed 32.3% of the labour force in 1980 (World Bank WDI archive, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/sources/57/country/YUG/series/SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS/time/YR1980;YR1975?format=json&per_page=100); industrialised federation with a domestic arms industry.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment (s = 1 assumed: Yugoslavia was broadly self-sufficient in food). World Bank WDI Database Archives, version 1989 Apr, Yugoslavia SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS 1980 = 32.3% -> 0.68 (mid); 1975 = 41.0% -> 0.59; CIA World Factbook 1990: 22% in agriculture (1986) -> 0.78. Low and high narrowed to 1978-82.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Men reaching military age per year. CIA World Factbook 1990: 188,028 males reach military age (19) annually (1990); the 1961 birth cohort reaching 19 in 1980 is assumed to be of similar size.

ifv_apc.note: The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru: 700 M-980 MICV on order (The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml): 500 on order) for delivery over several years: ~100 a year.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Galeb/Jastreb and later Orao (25 on order, The Military Balance 1981-82 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru (http://samlib.ru/t/temezhnikow_e_a/mb1981.shtml)) from the SOKO plant at Mostar.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Missile boats (8 FAC(M) on order, The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru), patrol craft and minesweepers from Adriatic yards.

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: 120,747 km of highways (1987; high), of which 71,315 km hard surface (low). Mid 110,000 allows for growth 1980-87.

railKm.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: 9,270 km of railways (1987; low, mid); high allows for lines closed 1980-87.

majorPorts.note: CIA World Factbook 1990: ports Rijeka, Split, Koper, Bar, Ploce (5), inland Belgrade (high 6). Naval bases Split (Lora), Pula, Sibenik, Ploce and Kotor (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru).

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Deadweight tonnage. CIA World Factbook 1990: 3,608,705 GRT / 5,809,219 DWT (1989; high); the 1980 fleet was smaller, no 1980 figure fetched.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Defensive war on interior lines with a motorised army; Territorial Defence depots in every commune.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses still used on private peasant farms; marginal for the army.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS stockpile series (OWID) lists no Yugoslav warheads.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: Total National Defence with 1M+ Territorial Defence and Dinaric mountains (The Military Balance 1980-81 (IISS), Yugoslavia entry, transcribed on samlib.ru); low 1.2 for the open Pannonian plain where a Warsaw Pact attack would come.

notes: Snapshot date mid-1980 (Military Balance 1980-81, with 1981-82 as the cross-check), months after Tito's death. Non-aligned federation with Soviet and Western equipment and a Total National Defence doctrine; the doctrine archetype is the regional mixed-equipment one. Weakest values: the P-role split, FROG launchers, merchant tonnage, roads in 1980, cohort and animals (educated guesses or later-year figures). Ship convention per SOURCES.md: destroyer and frigate ships_major; corvettes, missile and torpedo boats, patrol craft and minesweepers ships_minor; coastal Samlet batteries not counted.
